corrections.proposed: unresolved: register says circa 1934, but its description places the post in World War II
corrections.why: Volunteers were organized into the Aircraft Warning Service in May 1941, so a circa 1934 build date conflicts with the register's own WWII description.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says circa 1934; its description ties the post to World War II, and volunteers were organized into the Aircraft Warning Service in May 1941. Story reports the conflict and does not pick a date.

Register gives Foothill Ranch in one passage, local sources put it at Upper Drive just west of South Main Street, and some historical estimates place it around the corner of Chase and Main. Reported as unresolved.

notes_for_editor: The register files it with former fire lookouts but describes a WWII Aircraft Warning Service tower, so the story does not call it a fire lookout or a non-lookout (the brief's kind 'ground' fits). Only two sources were read: the register and Wikipedia. Two web searches found nothing on the post beyond the register, and the Corona Heritage museum page turned up in search without any AWS content. The 2018 exhibit reference is quoted from the register and was not checked directly. The NPS aircraft-warning PDF covers Joshua Tree, not Corona, and was not used. Suggest asking Corona Heritage Park & Museum about the post's location and any AWS records.
